rationale: The Latin anchors 'auxilium' (help/assistance) and 'remedium' (remedy) point to an activity or contribution of assistance rather than a person or a physical resource. Among the candidates, aid.n.02 ("the activity of contributing to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose") best captures the abstract sense of 'help' conveyed by BÓT in medical/remedial contexts (Lchdm. attestations), where it denotes the act of aiding or remedying a condition.
